content:
As a streaming service that prides itself on original content, Apple TV+ has been steadily expanding its catalog of exclusive shows and movies. But Apple is now adding some classic films to its service, available to subscribers for free streaming at no extra cost.

It remains unclear whether this new initiative is permanent or a limited-time promotion. The service attempted something similar a few years ago, but it did not last long.

You can find the current lineup in a new carousel within the Apple TV app called "Great Movies Now Available on Apple TV."

The specific selection varies by region, but we have seen availability in the United States, Canada, and the United Kingdom. The U.S. free movie lineup includes:

  • The Martian
  • Arrival
  • Spy Game
  • Looper
  • E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial
  • The Big Sick
  • I, Robot
  • Never Been Kissed
  • Dude, Where's My Car?
  • The Sixth Sense
  • Prisoners
  • Zoolander
  • Memories of Murder
  • Charlie's Angels
  • Titanic
  • Mission: Impossible – Ghost Protocol
  • A Beautiful Mind
  • The Aviator
  • Ten Thirty

These films would typically need to be purchased or rented on the Apple TV Store, but are now all labeled as "Just Released," available to stream for free with an Apple TV+ subscription. New subscribers can take advantage of a free seven-day trial. The standard monthly fee is $12.99, while the annual subscription costs $99. You can also access Apple TV+ through an Apple One bundle subscription.

Streaming is available via the native TV apps on iPhone, iPad, Mac, Android, and Windows devices, or through the web browser at tv.apple.com.

These newly added classics join a library of more than 300 original titles; you can see everything available to stream in our comprehensive guide. The service may have found more success with original series than with films.

The next original movie coming up is "Mayday," an action comedy starring Ryan Reynolds and Kenneth Branagh, set to premiere in September.
